files.lesson.md: --- order: 28 unit: rates node: AC9M8M05 n2 uses: [AC9M8M05 n1] title: Using rates summary: "Use a rate to find a total (rate × amount), or the amount (total ÷ rate). For speed: distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed. Show the units at every step, and check the answer makes sense." language: maths voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } hook: "How much will it cost to fill the car? How long is the drive to the coast? How many dollars for your holiday money? Each answer comes from one rate, used the right way round." connection: drip-rate app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-board" 8319 url: http://127.0.0.1:8319/index.html readySelector: "#gsum" layout: full explainPicture: { ref: rate.yml#explain-pic, caption: "At 70 km/h, 3 hours covers 210 km; 210 km ÷ 70 km/h gives back the 3 hours." } explainClip: query: { code: "@rate.yml#explain", fresh: 1, id: explain } caption: "Both ways along the line" say: "Multiply to find the distance. Divide to find the time." clip: - caption: { text: "At 70 km/h: 1 hour matches 70 km.", say: "Seventy kilometres per hour." } - wait: 800 - caption: { text: "3 hours: 70 × 3 = 210 km. And 210 ÷ 70 = 3 hours.", say: "Three hours is two hundred and ten kilometres. Divide to go back." } - click: Make the time bigger - click: Make the time bigger - click: Make the time bigger - click: Make the time bigger - expect: { selector: "#gsum", contains: "210 km" } - wait: 1500 --- A rate links two quantities, so you can go either way: - **total = rate × amount**: 30 L of petrol at $1.80 per L costs $30 × 1.80$ = \$54.00; - **amount = total ÷ rate**: \$54.00 at $1.80 per L buys $54 \div 1.80 = 30$ L. For speed, **distance = speed × time** and **time = distance ÷ speed**. Write the units at each step: they tell you whether to multiply or divide (km ÷ km/h = h). Then check: is the answer about the right size? The petrol prices and the exchange rate in this lesson are made up for the task. ## Predict: fill the tank ```step stage: predict insight: "Committing to a cost from a price per litre shows whether they multiply the rate by the amount." check: type: predict q: "Petrol costs $2.05 per litre. How much do 40 litres cost?" options: ["$82", "$19.51", "$42.05", "$8.20"] actual: "$82: 40 × $2.05 = $82. (40 ÷ 2.05 = 19.51 would be how many litres $40 buys.)" ``` ## Run: the petrol bowser ```step stage: run insight: "Moving the litres along the double number line shows the cost growing by the rate for every litre." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#run", height: 480 } check: { type: board, text: "Set 40 litres. Was your prediction right?", when: "x = 40", explain: "40 × $2.05 = $82." } ``` ## Investigate: multiply or divide ```step stage: investigate insight: "Units decide multiply or divide (Leo multiplies to find a time); currency conversion is a rate too." tasks: - check: type: number q: "How long does it take to drive 270 km at 90 km/h, in hours?" answer: 3 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["24300", "Time = distance ÷ speed."] explain: "270 ÷ 90 = 3 hours." - check: type: bug code: "working.txt#leo" text: "Leo works out a journey time. Click the line where his working goes wrong." answer: 2 fault: logic misconception: rate-multiply-divide explain: "Line 2: time = distance ÷ speed. 150 ÷ 60 = 2.5 hours. Units check: km ÷ km per h = h." - check: type: number q: "Say the exchange rate is 1 Australian dollar = 0.65 US dollars. How many US dollars do you get for 200 Australian dollars?" answer: 130 tolerance: 0 explain: "200 × 0.65 = 130 US dollars." ``` ### Time Here is the routine. ```worked \text{time} = \text{distance} \div \text{speed} :: Choose by the units: km ÷ km/h = h. 200 \div 80 = 2.5 :: Divide: 200 km at 80 km/h. 2.5 \text{ h} = 2 \text{ h } 30 \text{ min} :: Interpret: half an hour is 30 minutes. 80 \times 2.5 = 200 :: Check by going back. ``` ### Find the mistake Read Leo's working. Do the units come out as hours? ### Exchange rates ## Modify: race, shower, money back ```step stage: modify insight: "Comparing two rates over time, working backwards from a total, and converting money both ways." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#race", height: 560 } tasks: - starter: "rate.yml#race" hint: ["Car B gains 15 km every hour.", "45 ÷ 15 = ?"] check: { type: board, text: "Two cars leave together at 60 km/h and 75 km/h. When is Car B 45 km ahead?", when: "x = 3", explain: "B gains 75 − 60 = 15 km each hour: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours." } - check: type: number q: "With the same example rate (1 Australian dollar = 0.65 US dollars), how many Australian dollars are 52 US dollars worth?" answer: 80 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["33.8", "Going back the other way: divide by 0.65."] explain: "52 ÷ 0.65 = 80 Australian dollars." - starter: "rate.yml#shower" check: { type: board, text: "A shower uses 9 L per minute. How long is a shower that uses 72 L?", when: "y = 72", explain: "72 ÷ 9 = 8 minutes." } - check: type: number q: "A tap drips 0.5 L every hour. How many litres does it waste in a week?" answer: 84 tolerance: 0 explain: "A week is 24 × 7 = 168 hours: 168 × 0.5 = 84 L." ``` ### Catch up ### Money back ### A shower ### A dripping tap ## Practise: using rates ```step stage: practise insight: "Totals, distances, times and a conversion, mixed; multiplying when the units say divide is the planted slip; the speed conversion review keeps units fresh." tasks: - check: type: number q: "Grapes cost $4.20 per kg. How much do 3.5 kg cost, in dollars?" answer: 14.7 tolerance: 0 explain: "3.5 × 4.20 = $14.70." - check: type: number q: "A bus averages 85 km/h for 2.5 hours. How far does it go, in km?" answer: 212.5 tolerance: 0 explain: "85 × 2.5 = 212.5 km." - check: type: number q: "A cyclist rides 45 km at 15 km/h. How many hours does it take?" answer: 3 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["675", "Time = distance ÷ speed."] explain: "45 ÷ 15 = 3 hours." - check: type: number q: "Review: convert 72 km/h to metres per second." answer: 20 tolerance: 0 explain: "72 ÷ 3.6 = 20 m/s." - check: type: number q: "A part-time job pays $18.50 per hour. How much is 6.5 hours of work, in dollars?" answer: 120.25 tolerance: 0 explain: "18.50 × 6.5 = $120.25." - check: type: number q: "A cricket team needs 120 runs off the last 15 overs. What run rate (runs per over) does it need?" answer: 8 tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["1800", "A rate per over divides: runs ÷ overs."] explain: "120 ÷ 15 = 8 runs per over." ``` ### Cost ### Distance ### Time ### Review: m/s ### Pay ### Run rate ## Make: plan a drive ```step stage: make insight: "Choosing a speed and time for a fixed distance uses distance = speed × time in both directions." try: { playground: board, starter: "rate.yml#trip", height: 520 } hint: ["360 ÷ 4.5 = ?", "The time is 4 and a half hours."] check: { type: board, text: "A 360 km drive must take 4.5 hours. Set the speed and time.", when: "y = 360 and x = 4.5", explain: "360 ÷ 4.5 = 80 km/h." } ``` Then say whether your speed is a sensible average for a country drive with a stop, and what the model leaves out. ## Make: a drip rate, on paper ```step stage: make insight: "Two rates chained: mL per hour, then drops per hour, then drops per minute. The units say what to multiply and what to divide." hint: ["Divide the volume by the hours first.", "Then use the drop factor, then change hours to minutes."] check: type: reasoning paper: true q: "A drip must give 600 mL over 4 hours through a set that makes 20 drops from every mL. How many drops a minute is that?" steps: - ["$600 \\div 4 = 150$ mL each hour", "volume divided by time is a rate in mL per hour"] - ["$150 \\times 20 = 3000$ drops each hour", "mL per hour times drops per mL: the mL cancel, leaving drops per hour"] - ["$3000 \\div 60 = 50$ drops each minute", "an hour is 60 minutes, so divide to get a rate per minute"] - ["Check: $50 \\times 240 = 12\\,000$ drops, and $600 \\times 20 = 12\\,000$", "the minutes in 4 hours times the rate matches the total drops"] picks: - step: 2 q: "Why multiply 150 by 20?" options: - "Each mL makes 20 drops, so mL per hour times drops per mL gives drops per hour" - "Divide by 20, because a drop is smaller than a mL" - "Multiply by 60 first, to change hours to minutes" answer: 0 feedback: [null, "A drop is smaller, so there are more drops than mL. Multiply.", "Changing to minutes is the last step, and it divides."] answer: "50" answerLabel: "Drops a minute" tolerance: 0 feedback: - ["3000", "That is drops an hour. The question asks per minute: divide by 60."] - ["150", "That is mL an hour. Turn mL into drops with the 20 drops per mL."] criteria: - "I wrote the units at every step." - "I chained the rates: mL an hour, drops an hour, drops a minute." - "I checked the total number of drops." explain: "600 ÷ 4 = 150 mL an hour, × 20 = 3000 drops an hour, ÷ 60 = 50 drops a minute." ``` Do this one in your book, not on the screen. The volume and the time are made up for the task, not for real care. Write the units at every step: they tell you whether to multiply or divide. Then type the answer. **Also used in** - **Shopping.** Two packs of cereal, 500 g for \$4.80 or 750 g for \$6.60 (made-up prices): the price per 100 g, 96 c or 88 c, shows which is better value. - **Health.** A nurse checks a drip by chaining rates by hand, as here. - **Travel.** Fuel, speed and exchange rates are all one rate used the right way round. ```teacher summary: Students use rates both ways (total = rate × amount, amount = total ÷ rate) for petrol, speed, water and exchange rates, letting the units decide multiply or divide (AC9M8M05, node 2). time: 35 timing: Predict and Run 8 min · Investigate 8 min · Modify 10 min · Practise and Make 9 min goals: - I can use a rate to find a total or an amount. - I can use distance, speed and time in any order. - I can check an answer with its units and its size. struggle: Choosing to multiply or divide. Ask students to write the units into the calculation (km ÷ km/h = h) before they press a key. before: > Do the Run board yourself first. Students need rates and unit rates (previous lesson). The one idea: a rate works both ways; the units decide whether to multiply or divide. The common mistake is multiplying distance by speed to find a time (Leo's mistake). The exchange rate in the lesson (0.65 US dollars per Australian dollar) is a round example, not today's rate. Wider: plan holiday spending with a current exchange rate (and its fees); compare two phone plans. running: - "Predict: ask what 40 ÷ 2.05 would mean." - "Run: ask how much one more litre adds." - "Investigate: ask Leo whether 9000 hours makes sense." - "Modify: ask why the gap grows by the same amount each hour." - "Make: ask what the model leaves out." - "Paper: the drip-rate task in Make is worked in books; the page marks the answer (50) and the reason for multiplying by the drop factor. Books out, then look for the units written beside each step." stuck: - see: A student multiplies to find a time. ask: What units does your answer have? fix: "km ÷ km/h gives hours: divide." - see: A student writes 2.5 hours as 2 h 50 min. ask: What is half an hour in minutes? fix: 0.5 h = 30 min. - see: A student converts money the wrong way. ask: Should you get more or fewer US dollars than Australian dollars? fix: "Check the size: 1 AUD buys less than 1 USD here." stretch: "Plan a trip budget overseas: look up today's exchange rate, convert three prices, and include a 3% card fee." support: "A card: total = rate × amount; amount = total ÷ rate; units in every line." leads: > This completes AC9M8M05. Where it leads: rate models (next lessons), gradient as a rate (Linear relations), and speed in science. exit: q: A plane flies 2100 km at 700 km/h. How long does it take? a: 2100 ÷ 700 = 3 hours. explain: > Use a rate both ways: **total = rate × amount** and **amount = total ÷ rate**. For speed, distance = speed × time and time = distance ÷ speed. Write the units at each step (km ÷ km/h = h); they tell you whether to multiply or divide. Then check the size makes sense. ```

# region: leo
Leo drives 150 km at 60 km/h. How long does it take?
Time = distance × speed = 150 × 60.
So it takes 9000 hours.
